correctness.rationale: The standard internal angle-bisector identity gives \(w_c^2=ab((a+b)^2-c^2)/(a+b)^2\). As an interior point tends to \(C\), \(R_1\to b\), \(R_2\to a\), \(R_3\to0\), \(w_1,w_2\to0\), and \(w_3\to w_c\). Hence the defect tends exactly to \(b[ac^2-(a-b)(a+b)^2]/(a+b)^2\). The strict side condition makes this negative, and continuity supplies an actual open interior neighborhood of counterexamples. For \(a,b,c=(5,4,3)\), the limit is \(16-160/9=-16/9\). No finite numerical sampling is needed for the quantified conclusion.
risks: The displayed side inequality is sufficient, not claimed necessary; the size of the violating boundary layer is not optimized.
